'''David Hennessey Waldeck''' (September 5, 1956 – February 25, 2026) was an American chemist.

== Life and career ==
Waldeck was born in [[Cincinnati, Ohio]]. He attended the [[University of Cincinnati]], earning his [[Bachelor of Science|BS degree]] in 1978.<ref>{{Citation|title=ACS Directory of Graduate Research|date=1993|publisher=American Chemical Society|author=American Chemical Society. Committee on Professional Training}}</ref> He also attended the [[University of Chicago]], earning his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in [[chemistry]] in 1983. After earning his degrees, he worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.pitt.edu/news/mourning-passing-distinguished-professor-david-h-waldeck|title=Mourning the Passing of Distinguished Professor David H. Waldeck|work=[[University of Pittsburgh]]|access-date=March 17, 2026}}</ref>

Waldeck served as a professor in the department of chemistry at the [[University of Pittsburgh]] from 1985 to 2024. During his years as a professor, in 2004, he was named a [[List of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]], "for his fundamental contributions to the molecular and electronic origins of friction in chemical reactions and transport processes in liquid solutions",<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=waldeck&af=true|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=March 17, 2026}}</ref> and was named a [[distinguished professor]] in 2024.<ref name="b">{{Cite web|url=https://www.waldecklab.com/uploads/1/2/9/6/129684240/cv2025short_january.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae|date=December 2024|work=Waldeck Lab|access-date=March 17, 2026}}</ref><ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://www.utimes.pitt.edu/passings/david-waldeck-was|title=David Waldeck was ‘a towering figure in chemistry’|work=[[University of Pittsburgh]]|date=March 15, 2026|access-date=March 17, 2026}}</ref> In the same year, he co-authored the [[textbook]] ''Principles of Physical Chemistry'', which emphasizes a molecular-level understanding of chemical systems.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Kuhn |first1=Hans |last2=Försterling |first2=Horst-Dieter |last3=Waldeck |first3=David H. |title=Principles of Physical Chemistry |date=2024 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-1119904267 |edition=3rd}}</ref>

== Death ==
Waldeck died in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]] on February 25, 2026, at the age of 69.<ref name="a" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cen.acs.org/people/obituaries/Obituary-David-Waldeck/104/web/2026/04|title=Obituary: David Waldeck|work=Chemical & Engineering News|date=April 3, 2026|access-date=May 9, 2026}}</ref>
